draft.title: Latitude and longitude
card: Latitude
Lines of latitude run east to west, parallel to the equator. They measure how many degrees a place is north or south of the equator, which is 0 degrees.
Longitude
Lines of longitude run from the North Pole to the South Pole. They measure how many degrees a place is east or west of Greenwich in London, which is 0 degrees.
Each degree is split into 60 minutes. A position such as 33° 52′ S, 151° 12′ E is written with latitude first, then longitude.
The letters N, S, E and W tell you the side of the equator or Greenwich. Sydney is south of the equator and east of Greenwich, so it is S and E.
draft.remember: Latitude measures north or south of the equator. Longitude measures east or west of Greenwich.

a.q: A town is at 30° S, 150° E. What does the 150° E tell you?
opts: It is 150 degrees east of Greenwich
It is 150 degrees east of the equator
It is 150 degrees north of Greenwich
It is 150 degrees south of the equator
a.why: Longitude is measured east or west of Greenwich, so 150° E means 150 degrees east of Greenwich. Saying east of the equator mixes up the two, because the equator is the starting line for latitude.
a.clue: Which line is the starting point for longitude?

b.q: Priya writes the position of her school as 33° 45′ S, 150° 55′ E. Which statement about the position is correct?
opts: It is 33° 45′ south of the equator
It is 33° 45′ east of Greenwich
It is 150° 55′ south of the equator
It is 33 degrees and 45 degrees south
b.why: The first figure is latitude, so 33° 45′ S is 33 degrees and 45 minutes south of the equator. The option about 33° 45′ east of Greenwich mixes up the two, as longitude is the second figure. The last option treats minutes as degrees, but a degree is split into 60 minutes.
b.clue: Latitude comes first. Check what the letter S refers to.

a.best: It is 150 degrees east of Greenwich

b.best: It is 33° 45′ south of the equator

problems.detail: Why (b) refers to 'the last option' as the one that treats minutes as degrees. Options are shown in random order, and in this order the last option is '150° 55′ south of the equator', not '33 degrees and 45 degrees south'. The why should name the option by its content. It also never explains why the '150° 55′ south' option is wrong.
